question.text: While briefing an FPE's treasury team on SSE prerequisites, the SIA distinguishes the Money Market from the Securities Market. Which statement accurately captures the distinction?

answer.text: Money market instruments have maturities ranging from overnight to one year (repo, T-bills, CPs, CDs); securities/capital markets trade longer-tenure equity and debt instruments
Money market deals only with foreign currency; securities market deals only with domestic currency
Money market is regulated by SEBI while securities market is regulated by RBI
Money market trades derivatives exclusively; securities market trades only equity shares

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Money market instruments include repos/reverse repos, certificates of deposits, T-bills, and commercial papers with maturities up to one year. The securities market (capital market) has a primary segment (new issues) and a secondary segment (stock exchange trading) for longer-tenure equity and debt. **The Trap:** Option B conflates forex and money markets. Option C swaps regulators — RBI regulates money market, SEBI regulates securities market (with overlaps). Option D is fabricated. **Cross-Exam Context:** Cross-links to XII (Securities Markets Foundation). SIAs use this distinction when understanding how SSE-listed SEs interact with wider capital markets — SSE is a segment of the securities market. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** When the SE treasury discusses interim parking of ZCZP proceeds in CPs/T-bills, flag to audit: money-market parking must still be within the 'objects clause' and within ZCZP-utilization timelines. Document yield-earned and how it was recycled into the project.
